# PR #4473: Patch: a job ran over 10 minutes

Closes #4462

## What changed and why

`rust (test tools, wasm 1/4)` ran 11m 51s. I reproduced the shard exactly as CI builds it (workspace minus engine/cards/server/ai, `--skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions::`: 2014 tests, shard 1/4 = 506) and timed every suspect. The long pole is again fork_screen's r4397000 cap test: 209 s alone, and the `jackioh` bin took 267.63 s of the ~315 s shard wall. The other ~500 tests are diffuse (next-biggest: sweep/gate/arena/stats combined 99.5 s; perf smoke 12 s; golden 8 s).

The preferred trim cannot work here, so I took the plan's diffuse branch: `"tools, wasm" = 4` to `= 8` in [scripts/ci-shards.toml](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-4462/scripts/ci-shards.toml) (comment records #4462 and why), the most `matrix.py` allows. No Rust touched, no test skipped, weakened, renamed or added.

## How I tested it

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude ... -- --exact $(cat /tmp/shard1.txt)` (shard 1/4 baseline): green, `jackioh` bin 123 passed in 267.63 s; all other binaries seconds.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- <cap test> --exact`: 209.34 s alone. Over the 120 s bar, but at its floor (see below).
- New worst shard holds the cap test (5/8, 255 tests): `cargo test ... -- --exact $(cat /tmp/shard5-8.txt)` green, 254 passed, 1 ignored, bin long pole 239.74 s, rest ≤2 s. All eight shard files sum to 2011 names, each exactly once.
- `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` lists `tools, wasm 1/8` through `8/8`; all other groups byte-identical (the pin-test diff proves it).
- `cargo fmt --check` green; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
- Group `--doc` step runs zero tests, so shard 1 carries no extra run load.
- `python3 -m unittest bot.tests.test_ci_matrix`: 13/15 pass; the 2 failures are only the stale `JOBS` pin (expected-red until the person co-lands it; line 112's `len(JOBS)+3` heals itself once `JOBS` grows).

## Decisions the task did not settle

- Count 8 instead of trimming. Rejected the trim: the cap test is at its floor — 32 arms = 2 thread pools × 16, and the one-vs-four comparison is the test's point; its trunk plays via `par_iter`, so two games to one saves ~0 wall; pairs come from the production `FORK_ROLLOUTS` constant. The deepest honest cut saves seconds, while Step 4's 250 s bar exceeds the whole test (209 s). Dropping a pool would weaken per-PR coverage of thread-determinism. Departure from the plan to record: Step 5's gate says "no test over 120 s", but a >120 s test exists — Step 5 was taken anyway because its intent (trim can't fix it, re-shard) is met and measured.
- 8 rather than 6: any count ≠4 needs the person's pin equally, so take the cap; it also minimizes every non-cap shard.
- No Rust change at all, not even the trivial trunk cut: zero wall effect means pure churn, and #4441's workload-pinning assert stays valid untouched.
- No local cold-compile measurement for the group-split question: a 2-CPU box can't reproduce CI's compile/cache, so that call stays with the person's measurement (below).

## Reviewer, look twice at

- The toml comment's claims: "209 s alone" (dev profile, 2 CPUs), "trunk plays in parallel" (`play_trunk` uses `par_iter`), "pools are the test's point" (one-vs-four byte-identity assert). All verified above.
- Shard-integrity rests on hash-by-name (no renames) plus the green `ShardTests`; the pin diff touches only `tools, wasm` entries.

## A person must still do two things

1. Required: co-land the pin (`bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`, exact diff in the plan's Open questions: JOBS comment/`1/8`..`8/8` lines, shard-tuple set, filter assert). `bot selftest` stays red until then.
2. If their measurement shows compile won: the `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` tools/wasm group split (exact text in the plan's Open questions). Supporting evidence from here: shards 2–4/4 were near 10 min with only ~100–150 s of run each, so ~400 s+ of that job is compile and overhead; at count 8 the worst run-side shard is ~2 min on CI, leaving the shard at compile plus ~2 min.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| Round | Builder | Checks | Review |

| 1 | build, 72.2 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 8s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 530s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 5s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 9s |

</details>

   - `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py shard 1 4 < /tmp/tests.txt > /tmp/shard1.txt; wc -l /tmp/shard1.txt`
   - Copy the pattern from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `cargo test` step (list, hash-pick, `--exact` run): run `time cargo test --workspace --exclude jackioh-engine --exclude jackioh-cards --exclude jackioh-server --exclude jackioh-ai -- --exact $(cat /tmp/shard1.txt)` and record wall time plus the compile-vs-run split (compile ends where the `test result` lines start).
2. Find which tests sit in shard 1/4: `grep -o '^[a-z_]*::' /tmp/shard1.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn`. Expect game-playing modules (`fork_screen`, `sweep`, `gate`, `arena`, `stats`) to dominate.
3. Time each suspect module alone with `time`, one command each (all per-PR tests of the group, filters as in Step 1):

   - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- sweep::`
   - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- gate::`
   - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- arena::`
   - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- stats::`
   - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_smoke`
   - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test golden`
   - The dominant test is the single test or module over 120 s wall. Copy the #4441 pattern (`git show 709c303c0a -- crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`): halve its games/pairs/rollouts (e.g. two trunk games to one), keep every assertion byte-identical, and add a workload-pinning assert in the same test (e.g. `assert!(expected.contains(&format!("\"rollouts\":{}", jobs.len() * FORK_ROLLOUTS * 2)))`) so re-enlarging it fails the test. Numbers go in existing constants or a new `const` beside them (CLAUDE.md rule 9). If the dominant test's whole workload belongs in the daily run instead, mark it `#[ignore = "daily: <why>"]` naming the per-PR canary that keeps it, copying `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` line 98 or `crates/tools/tests/pool_probe.rs` line 157. Never name any kept test `fuzz`, `selfplay` or `positions` anywhere in its path (group filters would drop it; see `crates/shared/tests/host_fuzz.rs` header).
4. Re-run Step 1's timed shard command. If shard 1/4 wall drops by at least 250 s versus Step 1 (711 s to under about 460 s locally, giving headroom for runner noise), keep `"tools, wasm" = 4` and skip Step 5: no person needed.
5. Diffuse branch only (no test over 120 s): in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` replace lines 40-44 with a comment recording `#4462` (11m 51s on shard 1/4 at 4; 8 is `matrix.py`'s `MAX_SHARDS`) and `"tools, wasm" = 8`. Then run `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix 2>/dev/null | head -3` and confirm eight `tools, wasm k/8` jobs appear. Expect `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` to fail on its pin; that is the person's half (Open questions), flagged in the final report, not fixed by editing `bot/`.

## Tests

- No new test names: the trimmed test keeps its name and must pass with its new workload assert: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh <trimmed test path>` (e.g. `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh fork_screen::tests::r4397000_an_always_differing_candidate_forks_every_game_at_the_cap` if that is the one), plus the module run from Step 3.
- Shard-integrity: `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` still lists every group and the count change only renames `tools, wasm` shards; every name lands in exactly one shard for any count by construction (`matrix.shard` CRC-32).
- `cargo fmt --check`.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Do not run `cargo test --workspace`, whole web vitest, or e2e; V20 wire and `spec check` are unaffected (no generated types, no rulings touched).

## Done when

- [ ] Step 1-3 measurements recorded (shard 1/4 members, compile vs run split, dominant test and its wall time).
- [ ] Dominant test trimmed (or daily-marked with canary) with workload-pinning assert, targeted test and module runs green.
- [ ] Shard 1/4 reproduction at least 250 s faster, or count at 8 with eight jobs in matrix output.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` green.
- [ ] If the count moved: final report names the person-side pin diff (Open questions) as expected-red until co-landed.
- [ ] Every decision the task did not settle recorded with the rejected alternative.

## Risks

- Compile-dominated job: each shard recompiles the workspace subset (about 6 minutes estimated from #4441's 848 s at count 1); a count cannot fix that, hence Step 6 hands a group split to a person instead of burning runners up to the cap.
- Hash reshuffle: any test rename re-deals CRC-32 shards; the workload assert pins the fix to the test, not to shard luck.
- Pin redness: with count 8, `bot selftest` fails until the person co-lands the pin; say so in the report rather than touching `bot/`.
- Determinism: keep thread-count assertions (the #4441 one-thread-vs-four pattern) wherever rollouts use rayon's pool; keep `Rng`-seeded draws, never wall-clock.
- V20: every group checks `apps/web/src/wire` is unchanged; a pure test trim writes nothing there.

## Open questions

- Person-side pin for the diffuse branch (`bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`): in the comment on lines 25-27 change `` `tools, wasm` four since #4432 `` to `` `tools, wasm` eight since #4462 ``; line 33 becomes `"tools, wasm 1/8", "tools, wasm 2/8", "tools, wasm 3/8", "tools, wasm 4/8", "tools, wasm 5/8", "tools, wasm 6/8", "tools, wasm 7/8", "tools, wasm 8/8",`; line 85-86's `{(1, 1), (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4)}` becomes `{(1, 1), (1, 8), (2, 8), (3, 8), (4, 8), (5, 8), (6, 8), (7, 8), (8, 8)}`; line 87's `jobs["tools, wasm 1/4"]` becomes `jobs["tools, wasm 1/8"]`. Needed only if Step 5 runs.
- Person-side compile split for the Step 6 contingency (`.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, replacing the `tools, wasm` group at lines 170-174; both halves reuse scope `tools_wasm` so `scripts/ci-scope.sh` needs no change):
  `[[group]] group = "tools" scope = "tools_wasm" cache = "tools-wasm" test = "-p jackioh-tools -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions::"` and `[[group]] group = "wasm" scope = "tools_wasm" cache = "tools-wasm" test = "-p jackioh-run -p jackioh-shared -p jackioh-wasm -p jackioh-wasm-core -p jackioh-wasm-c -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions::"`. Optionally append `--config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=1 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=0` to either half if the person's measurement shows compile won and run time barely moves.
